To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conspicuous psychiatric morbility of a population is the number of patients who are seen by a doctor who is employed by a deputation service providing out‐ of‐hours medical attention.

the conspicuous psychiatric morbity of the 500 patients was 8% (95% confidence interval 5%‐11%), the conspicuous psychiatric morbility of patients with a medical problem was 8% and the conspicuous psychiatric morbidty of patients with an injury or a minor illness was 6% (95% CI 1%‐11%).

the conspicuous psychiatric morbility of a population of patients who are attended to by a doctor working in a deputizing out‐of‐ hours service is 8%, and that the total psychiatric morbility of this same population is 12%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the psychiatric morbidity of the population as a whole, rather than the conspicuous psychiatric morbity.
the psychiatric morbidity of an out‐of‐hour service.
the psychiatric morbidity in an out‐of‐ hours deputizing service.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the psychiatric morbidity of the general population, as determined by the doctor who is employed by a deputation service, is low.
8% of the population seen by the doctor in the deputizing service was suffering from a psychiatric disorder.
8% of patients presenting to a deputizing doctor have psychiatric problems, and that 2% have problems which are so conspicuous as to be obvious to the doctor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the psychiatric morbidity of the population is 8% but that only 2.5% of the total psychiatric morbidiy is conspicuous.

a deputizing doctor, who is not a psychiatrist, can be expected to encounter a psychiatric patient on average once in every six visits, and that this patient may have to be seen by the deputizing doctor on more than one occasion.

a doctor employed by a de‐putizing service, visiting patients in their own homes at night, is not likely to find many patients with psychiatric illness who need immediate treatment, and is not likely to be confronted by a large number of patients with psychiatric illness in whom he is unable to make a diagnosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the psychiatric morbidity of the general population is high.
the psychiatric morbidity is high in patients with chronic diseases.
, in the future, we need to be more proactive in our approach to mental health and well-being.
